## Publication

**A. Nema**, X. Zhou, A. J. Jillella, S. Zhao, and S. Liu. "Context-Aware and Knowledge-Grounded Conversational Recommendation with Prompt Learning." In *PRICAI 2025: Trends in Artificial Intelligence*, Lecture Notes in Computer Science, Springer Nature.

[Read the Springer chapter](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-981-95-7078-2_26)

## Summary

This paper focuses on conversational recommender systems, where the challenge is not only predicting what a user might like, but doing so through a natural dialogue that remembers context and can explain recommendations. The proposed framework, GraphPromptCRS, combines recommendation and response generation with a frozen LLM while using soft prompt learning to encode task-specific signals without full model fine-tuning.

The core idea is to use external knowledge and dialogue context together instead of treating each recommendation as an isolated prediction. A GraphRAG-based pipeline builds knowledge graphs from dialogue history, while a Community Prompt Enhancer captures topical user preferences. Experiments on the ReDial dataset show improvements in recommendation accuracy and conversational diversity against baselines.

## Why It Matters

Conversational recommendation is useful in domains such as e-commerce, media discovery, travel planning, and service support, where users refine their needs over multiple turns. A system that can track intent, retrieve relevant knowledge, and generate grounded responses can feel less like a static search filter and more like a helpful assistant.

## Portfolio Relevance

This project connects my interests in large language models, recommendation systems, retrieval, and user-centered AI. It also reflects the kind of applied AI work I enjoy most: systems that combine machine learning with usable interaction design and clear decision support.
